text: 在 DSH 主机启动并等待配置的 settle 时间后，插件扫描最近的持久化会话：目标状态仍为 active 时恢复会话并重新启用目标轮次；中断中的非目标会话只记录可直接使用的恢复命令。它会跳过已正常结束、超过过期窗口或当前仍在运行的会话，并限制每次启动的扫描数量与自动恢复数量，减少重复处理并按配置执行。

At DSH startup, scans recent persisted sessions and resumes sessions whose goal remains active, re-arming the goal rounds. Interrupted sessions without an active goal are logged with a ready-to-use resume command; clean, stale, and live sessions are skipped.
DSH 重新打开后，能不能接着跑之前还在进行的目标？
我想找出关闭应用时卡在半途的会话，并拿到恢复命令。
让 DSH 下次启动时自动恢复仍处于 active 状态的目标会话。
dsh-session-auto-resume 的功能「启动时恢复会话」：主机启动等待配置的时间后扫描近期持久化会话；仍为 active 的目标会显式恢复并重新启用目标轮次，中断的非目标会话则写入可直接使用的恢复命令。

@local/dsh-session-auto-resume README · dsh-session-auto-resume：A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that **automatically resumes agent sessions interrupted by app closure**. When the DSH host relaunches, sessions that were mid-work at closure are detected from persisted state and recovered without human action:

@local/dsh-session-auto-resume README · Why：The desktop host has quit-time inspection of active work but **no startup recovery path**: after any closure (crash, SIGTERM, deliberate quit/reload), interrupted sessions stay interrupted until a human notices. This plugin closes that gap entirely outside the app bundle, so it survives app updates.
@local/dsh-session-auto-resume README · Live verification：Tested against a real closure-then-relaunch cycle (operator-approved SIGTERM of the running host; app relaunched):

@local/dsh-session-auto-resume README · Live verification：`verify-d1.mjs` (included) turns any future closure into a one-command verdict: `PASS` (exit 0) / `FAIL` (exit 1, names the broken check + evidence tail) / `VOID` (exit 2, no closure recorded after the plugin armed). Its own fixture selftest (`verify-d1.test.mjs`) exercises every verdict path against synthetic evidence trees.

@local/dsh-session-auto-resume README · Design notes：- **Policy is explicit and minimal**: only durable goal phase `active` auto-resumes; paused/blocked goals are deliberate human states and are never re-armed; non-goal sessions are surfaced only. The plugin's installation *is* the one-time authorization.
- **Resume mirrors the harness's own resume flow** (`agents.resume({resumeSessionId, agentOptions, setup})` + `goals.resume(agent, {id, revision})`), including binding the default model — a resume without a model binding produces turns failing with `prompt variable "{{model}}" has no value` (the agent loop binds that variable from `agent.options`). This plugin binds it and logs a loud `resume-no-model` line if it cannot.
- **It never hand-appends to session logs.** Session-log append contracts (`headerSeq` must reference an earlier request/header) make cold-log markers unsafe; detection is recorded in the plugin's own log instead.
- **Fail-closed everywhere**: goal resume throws on exhausted budgets or invalid phase transitions (caught, logged, never retried); the boot pass, classification, logging, and resume are each guarded so a plugin failure cannot block host boot.

@local/dsh-session-auto-resume README · Install (as a local profile plugin)：3. The package's own `cordis.patch.yml` carries the required insert row (a bundles-list entry alone is silently skipped). It ships with `dryRun: true` — the first boot logs `would-resume` decisions without acting; verify them against your live sessions, then set `dryRun: false`.
4. Restart the app. Evidence lands in `~/.dsh/logs/session-auto-resume.log` (`ARMED` on every activation, one `pass-done` per boot).

@local/dsh-session-auto-resume README · Test：```sh
node selftest.mjs        # classification truth table, fake-ctx passes, mutation checks
node verify-d1.test.mjs  # proves verify-d1 on every verdict path (synthetic fixtures)
```
